blockers.message: the review record has no `## plan.challenge` section, while roles were active at it
R-privacy-1 (Looked-up e-mail address written to the error log) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it
R-privacy-2 (Chat vendor receives phone, birth date and address beyond the greeting purpose) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it

findings.evidence: throw new NotFoundError(`no customer with e-mail ${email}`);
findings.recommendation: Drop the e-mail from the message (`no customer for this e-mail`). The existing `errorHandler` (src/server.ts:14) logs `err.message`, so every lookup that finds nobody writes the typed e-mail address to the error log, breaking "no personal data goes to logs" (GDPR Art. 5(1)(c), 32). If a correlation is needed, log the customer-free request id instead.
findings.title: Looked-up e-mail address written to the error log

findings.evidence:
id: String(customer.id),
name: customer.name,
email: customer.email,
phone: customer.phone,
birthDate: customer.birth_date,
address: customer.address,
findings.recommendation: The proposal's purpose is that the Helply widget greets the customer by name so the agent knows who they talk to: send `id` and `name` only (and `email` only if the team states why the widget needs it). Phone, birth date and postal address go to a third-party processor with no stated use (GDPR Art. 5(1)(c) data minimisation, Art. 25, Art. 28). Also stop selecting the unused columns in `customerById` (line 28).
findings.title: Chat vendor receives phone, birth date and address beyond the greeting purpose

findings.evidence: "SELECT id, email, name, phone, birth_date, address FROM customers WHERE lower(email) = lower($1)",
findings.recommendation: The lookup's stated purpose is that agents stop asking customers who they are; the endpoint (src/routes.ts:7) returns the whole record, birth date included. Return only the fields the support console needs, or confirm with the team that agents need each of them (Art. 5(1)(c)).
findings.title: Lookup returns birth date, phone and address to support agents

findings.evidence: - [x] personal-data — customers' records are read and the chat vendor receives who is chatting
findings.recommendation: Question for the team: is Helply covered by a processing agreement (Art. 28), recorded in the records of processing (Art. 30), and does it host data outside the EEA (Chapter V)? State the lawful basis for sending customer data to it. Only the controller can answer.
findings.title: Helply as processor and its transfer location not identified
